text.p: IG Metall, Germany's largest trade union, on Friday insisted that it was staying out of talks scheduled between Chancellor Helmut Kohl and other union representatives on how to solve the country's jobless problem.
"We are not prepared to take part in whatever political sham lies behind these talks," a spokesman for the metal and engineering union said in response to enquiries.
Kohl's Christian Democrats have in recent weeks repeated calls for employer and union leaders to meet Kohl to discuss ways of halving the country's post-war record four million jobless total.

But IG Metall has rejected such talks after what it sees as Kohl's failure to keep promises made within the so-called "Alliance for Jobs" pact that followed similar talks between unions, employers and politicians early last year.

Dieter Schulte, the head of Germany's Federation of Trade Unions (DGB), met to discuss unemployment with Kohl around a week ago and a further meeting is, according to the DGB, scheduled for the middle of next month.

But the absence of representation from the three-million-member IG Metall, whose chairman Klaus Zwickel was a key player in the failed "Alliance for Jobs" scheme, will mean any agreements emerging from the talks have less weight.

The IG Metall spokesman said such talks were pointless because it was clear that the Bonn coalition were following policies that went against the creation of jobs. The discussions served only an "alibi function" for them, he added.

Kohl's government has been accused of attacking the welfare state and taking money out of the pockets of the least well-off in its drive to cut state deficits ahead of the single European currency set for 1999.
A spokesman for the DGB said however that the seriousness of the unemployment problem meant that communications channels had to remain open between government and unions.
IG Metall believes the fastest way to create jobs in Germany is to reduce overtime and the working week, something neither Kohl nor employers have expressed a willingness to allow.
